subject: physics
title: Model Question Paper 1
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 80 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–16 are MCQs (1 mark each). Questions 17–28 have two parts of 1 mark each.
Section B: 2-mark answers in 30–50 words, 3-mark answers in 50–80 words, 5-mark answers in 80–120 words. Show the working in numerical questions.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: The change in momentum of a body is equal to —
If the speed of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy increases by —
questions.work: K ∝ v². Doubling v makes K four times, i.e. an increase of 4K − K = 3K = 300%.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The efficiency of a reversible heat engine does not depend on the nature of the ______. (b) 1 kilocalorie = ______ J.
Complete using (ultraviolet rays, gamma rays, heat waves, radio waves): (a) Radiations with wavelength shorter than X-rays are ______. (b) Infrared rays are also called ______.
State True or False: (a) A dipole in a uniform field experiences no net force. (b) Charge is quantized.
questions.answer:
(a) True — only a torque.
(b) True — q = ne.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: How does an electric dipole behave in a non-uniform electric field?
questions.answer: The forces on its two charges are unequal, so it feels a net force (it moves towards the stronger field when aligned) as well as a torque that tends to align it with the field.

questions.q: The Q–V graphs of two capacitors X and Y are straight lines, X being steeper. Which stores more energy at the same voltage?
questions.answer: The slope Q/V = C, so X has the larger capacitance. U = ½CV², so at the same V, X stores more energy.

questions.q: Why do free electrons in a conductor not produce magnetism when there is no p.d.?
questions.answer: Their thermal motion is random in all directions, so the average (drift) velocity is zero. There is no net current, and hence no net magnetic field.

questions.q: Name the two fields produced around a moving charge. Are they in the same direction?
questions.answer: An electric field and a magnetic field. No — the magnetic field is perpendicular to the electric field (it circles round the line of motion).

questions.q: State Lenz's law. Show that it follows from conservation of energy.
questions.answer: The induced current flows in a direction that opposes the change producing it. If it aided the change, a small motion would produce ever-growing current and energy from nothing; opposing it means work must be done, which becomes electrical energy.

questions.q: What are anti-Stokes lines?
questions.answer: In the Raman spectrum, anti-Stokes lines are scattered lines of higher frequency (shorter wavelength) than the incident light. The photon gains energy from a molecule already in an excited vibrational state.

or.q: What is dispersion of light? Would you prefer a small-angled or a large-angled prism to produce dispersion?
or.answer: Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its colours because μ varies with wavelength. A large-angled prism, since angular dispersion (μ_v − μ_r)A increases with the angle A.

questions.q: In Young's experiment, how is a dark fringe produced on the screen?
questions.answer: Where the waves from the two slits arrive with a path difference of (2n − 1)λ/2 (a phase difference of an odd multiple of π), crest meets trough and they cancel, giving darkness.

or.q: In a single-slit diffraction pattern, what can you say about the width of the central fringe and the intensity of the bright fringes?
or.answer: (a) The central bright fringe is twice as wide as each of the others. (b) Its intensity is greatest, and the intensity of the later bright fringes falls off rapidly.

questions.q: Write two postulates of Rutherford's atomic model.
questions.answer:
(1) All the positive charge and nearly all the mass of an atom are concentrated in a tiny central nucleus.
(2) Electrons revolve round the nucleus in orbits, the electrostatic attraction providing the centripetal force; most of the atom is empty space.

questions.q: Radiation of frequency 5.6 × 10¹⁴ Hz releases photoelectrons with zero kinetic energy. Calculate the work function. (h = 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ J s)
questions.answer: This is the threshold frequency: φ = hν₀ = 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ × 5.6 × 10¹⁴ = 3.7 × 10⁻¹⁹ J ≈ 2.3 eV.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Two masses of 2 kg and 3 kg hang from a light string over a frictionless pulley. Find the acceleration and the tension. (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.answer:
a = (m₂ − m₁)g/(m₁ + m₂) = (3 − 2) × 9.8/5 = 1.96 m/s².
T = 2m₁m₂g/(m₁ + m₂) = 2 × 2 × 3 × 9.8/5 = 23.5 N.
The 3 kg mass moves down and the 2 kg mass moves up.

questions.q: A transformer is to run machines needing (i) 25000 V and (ii) 25 V from a 250 V, 50 Hz supply. Name the transformers and give their turns ratios.
questions.answer:
(i) Step-up transformer, Nₚ : Nₛ = 250 : 25000 = 1 : 100.
(ii) Step-down transformer, Nₚ : Nₛ = 250 : 25 = 10 : 1.
The primary is connected to the supply and the secondary to the machine.

questions.q: Name the series of the hydrogen spectrum with their regions and the formula for each.
questions.answer:
1/λ = R(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²):
Lyman — n₁ = 1, ultraviolet.
Balmer — n₁ = 2, visible.
Paschen — n₁ = 3, infrared.
Brackett — n₁ = 4, infrared.
Pfund — n₁ = 5, far infrared.
In each series n₂ = n₁ + 1, n₁ + 2, …

questions.q: Distinguish between nuclear fission and nuclear fusion.
questions.answer:
Fission: a heavy nucleus splits into lighter ones; triggered by slow neutrons at ordinary temperatures; can be controlled (reactors); produces radioactive waste.
Fusion: light nuclei combine into a heavier one; needs about 10⁷ K; occurs in the sun and stars; not yet controlled for power; gives more energy per unit mass and less radioactive waste.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain Einstein's photoelectric equation. How do the graph of stopping potential against frequency for two metals give the threshold frequency, work function and Planck's constant?
questions.answer:
Light consists of photons of energy hν. A photon gives all its energy to one electron, which spends φ = hν₀ to escape, so KE_max = hν − φ, i.e. eV₀ = hν − hν₀.
The graph of V₀ against ν is a straight line V₀ = (h/e)ν − φ/e.
Its intercept on the ν-axis is the threshold frequency ν₀; the metal with the larger ν₀ has the larger work function φ = hν₀.
The slope h/e is the same for every metal, so h = e × slope.

questions.q: Explain with circuit diagrams how a p-n junction diode works in (i) forward and (ii) reverse bias, and draw its V–I characteristics.
questions.answer:
Formation: diffusion of electrons and holes across the junction leaves a depletion layer with a barrier potential (Si about 0.7 V).
(i) Forward bias (p to +): the applied voltage opposes the barrier, the depletion layer narrows, majority carriers cross, and a large current flows after the knee voltage. Circuit: battery, diode, milliammeter, voltmeter and rheostat.
(ii) Reverse bias (p to −): the barrier rises and the depletion layer widens; only minority carriers give a tiny reverse current (µA), until breakdown. Circuit: battery reversed, with a microammeter.
Characteristic: a steep rise in the first quadrant after the knee; a small nearly flat current in the third quadrant, then a sudden rise at breakdown.
